question: Who among the following started the Khilafat Movement against the British government?

options.text: Syed Raza Ali and Muhammad Ali Jinnah
Maulana Mazharul Haque and Mian Abdul Aziz

solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khilafat Movement was launched in 1919 by **Shaukat Ali** and **Mohammad Ali**, popularly known as the Ali Brothers, to protest against the British government.
 
• The movement aimed to restore the position of the Ottoman Caliph, who was considered the spiritual leader of the Muslims worldwide.
 
• This movement was a significant part of India's freedom struggle, as it united Hindus and Muslims in a common cause against the British.
 
• It was closely linked to the Non-Cooperation Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, fostering Hindu-Muslim unity during that period.
 
• The movement lost momentum after the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in Turkey in 1924.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• The Ottoman Empire, led by the Caliph, was dismembered after World War I, and the Treaty of Sèvres (1920) further weakened the Caliph's position.
 
• Indian Muslims viewed the weakening of the Caliphate as a threat to their religious identity and sought to defend it.
 
 
 
• **Ali Brothers:**
 
 
• Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali were key leaders of the Khilafat Movement, actively organizing protests and rallies.
 
• Their leadership was instrumental in mobilizing the Muslim community across India.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, creating a broader base for anti-British sentiment.
 
• Both movements emphasized non-violent resistance against British policies.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Movement:**
 
 
• The abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924 marked the end of the Khilafat Movement's primary objective.
 
• Additionally, growing communal tensions in the 1920s weakened Hindu-Muslim unity, leading to the movement's decline.
